html:
The Inuvialuit, "the real people", are the Inuit of the western Canadian Arctic. Their homeland runs along the Arctic coast from the Alaska border east past the Mackenzie Delta and the Amundsen Gulf, and includes some of the western Arctic islands.

Like all Inuit they descend from the Thule, who spread east from Alaska. In 1492 they lived in large villages in the Mackenzie Delta, hunting beluga whales, seals and caribou. Their neighbours were the Inupiat to the west and the Gwich'in inland, with whom they traded and fought.

American whalers wintered at Herschel Island from the 1890s, and the diseases they brought, with later epidemics, killed most of the original Inuvialuit. Inupiat from Alaska moved in and joined them. In 1984 the Inuvialuit Final Agreement made them the first people in the Canadian Arctic to settle a modern land claim. Today they live in six communities, including Inuvik and Tuktoyaktuk.
